scope: Proposition 4.8 (Common exact lines) of the manuscript “Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation” (preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 145 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 45000cec6bcec95d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For almost every parameter square E, the following assertions hold simultaneously at all individual cells. 1. The orthogonal projections onto Va,j and Wa,j commute. Their common range Va,j ∩ Wa,j is spanned by the lines exact for both the full k-coordinate row law λpa and the full k-coordinate column law λqj . 2. For distinct columns s, t, let La s←t(v) be the row Markov operator from cell (a, t) to (a, s), conditioned on the remaining k − 2 row entries v. Then, for almost every v, PW a,sLa s←t(v) = La s←t(v)PW a,t . Column operators likewise intertwine the corresponding row-active projections. 3. If (χj)j∈I is an exact tuple for row a, with Q j χj(Ya,j) = c, then La s←t(v)χt = c Y j̸=s,t χj(vj) χs. (36) In particular, membership of one partner line in the column-active space is equivalent to membership of any other partner line in its column-active space. The analogous assertion holds with rows and columns exchanged.
